# Introduction
Now that I have packaged Circuity Database and uploaded it to PyPI I can import it as a Python dependency and use it programmatically.

# Functions
## Load dependencies
```{python}
#| code-fold: true

# Circuity database
import circuitydatabase as circuity

# Logging
import logging

# Manipulate files
import os
from pathlib import Path
# Read comma separated values file
import csv
# Manipulate the database structures
import json

# Manipulate lists
import random
import itertools
from operator import itemgetter
```

# Initialize database
## Create database structures
```{python}
csv_file_path = 'jaguars-offensive-players.csv'
```

## Populate database
```{python}
database = circuity.initialize_database()
database = circuity.import_comma_separated_values(database, csv_file_path)
```

# Example queries
## Get the age of a player by name
```{python}
query = 'parker washington age'
result = circuity.process_query(database, query)
result
```

## Get the position of a player by name
```{python}
query = 'parker washington position'
result = circuity.process_query(database, query)
result
```

## This one errors out
```
query = 'name wide receiver'
result = circuity.process_query(database, query)
result
```

## This one kind of works
All of these people are wide receivers except that not all of the wide receivers are listed and it includes their first and last names.
```{python}
query = 'wide receiver last name'
results = circuity.process_query(database, query)
",".join(results)
```

## This one also kind of works
There are (2) columns that include the word `height`: `height feet` and `height inches`. What I am looking for is a single result that includes both and instead I got (2) results that only include his height in feet.
```{python}
query = 'trevor lawrence height'
results = circuity.process_query(database, query)
",".join(results)
```

## This one errors out
`RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded`
```
query = 'trevor lawrence years of experience'
results = circuity.process_query(database, query)
",".join(results)
```

## This one kind of works
It returns his height in feet and inches and in an awkward order
```{python}
query = 'nick mullens height inches'
results = circuity.process_query(database, query)
",".join(results)
```

## This one returns (2) invalid results
```{python}
query = 'brown college'
results = circuity.process_query(database, query)
",".join(results)
```

## This returns (2) invalid results
The word "college" is in the name of "Boston College" which seems to be confounding the algorithm. 
```{python}
query = 'robert hainsey college'
results = circuity.process_query(database, query)
",".join(results)
```
